newsitem.title: UK: NORTH SEA CRUDES FRAGILE, COULD WEAKEN FURTHER.
newsitem.headline: NORTH SEA CRUDES FRAGILE, COULD WEAKEN FURTHER.

text.p: North Sea crudes were looking fragile on Friday and set for further losses in the absence of prompt refinery demand and caution over the resumption of Iraqi exports, traders said.
"There's a lot of uncertainty with regard to who will get what from Iraq and how much they plan to sell. We're expecting a very slow day," said a trader.

Sept Brent shed 12 cents to $18.78 a barrel by 1055 GMT, extending this week's slide which has knocked 88 cents off the price as the two main market props -- Iraq's absence and strong gasoline prices -- have crumbled.
Rotterdam gasoline barge prices were also on the skids, shedding some $13 a tonne and making refineries even more cautious about taking on more crude with margins looking vulnerable.
With the exception of the illiquid Aug/Sep intermonth spread, cash Brent market slipped deeper into contango, Sep/Oct offered at -17 cents after trade late on Thursday at -15 cents.
Brent CFDs also slipped lower, next week's Aug 11-15 dates talking at the equivalent of Oct Brent -40/-35 cents, five cents weaker. The following week dropped three cents to -36/-31 cents.
Four Brent cargoes were due to turn wet on Friday, traders said.
Other North Sea markets were quiet and stable but could suffer further under the weight of unsold late August cargoes.
"Refineries appear to be pretty well covered until the end of the month," said a trader.
Norwegian Statfjord and Oseberg were the most amply supplied but unlikely to collapse, said another.
"There are still some cargoes available but you shouldn't overestimate what's left," he said.
